phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 5; ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: (SID name and number) DEPARTURE, (transition name) TRANSITION, THEN AS FILED — used when the first filed fix after the SID is one of its published transitions

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 5; ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: (SID name and number) DEPARTURE, (fix), THEN AS FILED — used when the first filed fix after the SID is not one of its published transitions, including the SID's own base fix; the fix is spoken bare, without a facility word

A filed element the departure itself flies over — the SID's own name, the fix it is built on, or a fix it is restricted over — is not read back when the route files one of that same SID's published transitions further along: the route is read from that transition (R-TRANSITION) and the elements before it are dropped from the route box. Where the route files no published transition of the SID nothing is dropped and the first filed fix stands, spoken bare (R-AS-FILED)

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 5 / ZOA practice; ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: (SID name and number) DEPARTURE, RADAR VECTORS (fix), THEN AS FILED — used for radar-vector and vector-segment SIDs

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA practice relayed by the user, 2026-09-16
phraseologyRules.text: A radar-vector SID is filed as the SID, the departure airport's navaid, then the route (OAK6 OAK RBL, SFO5 SFO RBL) for the computerized flight plan; the navaid is not spoken. A route box that omits it is acceptable, not wrong

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference; user rule 2026-09-16 (N172SP amendment plan)
phraseologyRules.text: THEN AS FILED — only when the last fix spoken connects to the rest of the route the pilot filed: on an amended route the controller reads every element up to the first fix that was already on the filed plan and after which the two routes are identical, then THEN AS FILED; when no such fix exists, or nothing follows it, the route is read in full to the end

phraseologyRules.source: OAK Route Building Cheat Sheet (vZOA S1-OAK-5), retrieved 2026-09-16; user rules 2026-09-16 (SWA984 amendment plan) and 2026-09-17 (PXT415: WAGES LOSHN off SKYL1)
phraseologyRules.text: Before falling back to the vector SID or a heading, route-build: keep a SID the SOP assigns by connecting one of its published transitions, or the fix the SID itself ends on, to the filed route through fixes that connect, fewest changes first; a suboptimal route that is legal per the SOPs and LOAs is not an unclean route

phraseologyRules.source: AIM 5-1-6 b (the route of flight is described accurately and completely, by airways, jet routes, reporting points and NAVAIDs); FAA JO 7110.65 4-2-5; user rule 2026-09-17 (UAL313)
phraseologyRules.text: Every element of a filed route names a fix, a navaid, an airway or a procedure. An element that names none of them — two identifiers run together, or a typo — is removed from the route box and the fixes either side of it are connected through fixes that connect (R-ROUTE-BUILD), so the clearance reads a route the pilot can fly; where nothing connects them the element is dropped and the fixes either side of it join direct

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA Common ZLA Arrivals from ZOA (current as of 2025-01-13); ZOA-ZLA LOA Attachment 1 (effective 2026-04-26); user rules 2026-09-16 (SWA984: an RNAV jet filing the non-RNAV SADDE8 is put on IRNMN2 via BURGL; a missed arrival costs half a point) and 2026-09-17 (NKS510: a non-RNAV jet filing IRNMN2 is put on SKYL1 AVE SADDE8)
phraseologyRules.text: A departure is routed onto an arrival of its destination that its equipment can fly, RNAV or conventional, entered at a transition the common-arrivals table or the letter of agreement names where the route-building connections reach one, fewest changes first; the arrival is a nice-to-have the enroute controller can change on the fly, so a route box left on the arrival as filed costs half a point, not a full one

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 3; OAK ATCT SOP 2-1 c (via koak-v3 notes); S1-SFO-0 CBT No SID
phraseologyRules.text: VIA FLY RUNWAY HEADING / VIA TURN LEFT (or RIGHT) HEADING (heading), RADAR VECTORS (first fix), THEN AS FILED — a departure the SOP sends off without a DP is cleared on the runway heading, or turned the shorter way onto the heading the row names, and vectored to the first filed fix; no procedure is named

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: (SID name and number) DEPARTURE, RADAR VECTORS TO JOIN (airway), THEN AS FILED — used when the first filed element after the SID is an airway

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 2-5-1; ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference; user review 2026-09-15; user steer 2026-09-17 (pacing comma)
phraseologyRules.text: Airways are spoken as the word VICTOR or TANGO, or the letter J or Q, followed by the number in group form (Victor two forty-four, Jay five thirty-three, Queue one seventy-four, Tango two ten); other route letters phonetically; a comma follows the airway before the fix it leads to, for pacing (Queue one seventy-four, Flchr), where DIRECT (fix) takes none

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 2-5-2; ZOA practice (S1-OAK-2 knowledge check: RADAR VECTORS LINDEN VOR); user review 2026-09-15
phraseologyRules.text: A navaid in a clearance is spoken by name followed by its facility type; VOR, VOR/DME and VORTAC are all VOR (Sacramento VOR, Red Bluff VOR); transitions keep their published name

phraseologyRules.source: AIM 5-3-4 c 1
phraseologyRules.text: A published RNAV route is filed only by an aircraft with the navigation it needs: a Q route by an RNAV-capable aircraft (GPS or DME/DME/IRU), a T or Y route by a GPS-equipped one; a non-RNAV aircraft files a conventional airway or a navaid route instead

phraseologyRules.source: AIM 5-3-4 c 1; ARINC 424 enroute waypoint type (CIFP)
phraseologyRules.text: A fix the CIFP publishes as an RNAV waypoint is filed only by an RNAV-capable aircraft; a combined fix that is also a named intersection, and a navaid, need no RNAV

phraseologyRules.source: VATSIM Code of Conduct B4(a); VATSIM transponder simulation (standby or Mode A+C only); user, 2026-09-17
phraseologyRules.text: Every aircraft on VATSIM simulates a Mode C transponder, so an equipment suffix without Mode C (/X, /T, /D, /B, /M, /N, /Y, /C, /V, /S, /H, /O) is not filed on the network; the type box carries the suffix the fleet files for the type

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 4 (a); ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: CLIMB VIA SID — the SID has published crossing restrictions and its published top altitude is the altitude ATC wants; at KSFO this is the form for a SID that publishes a top altitude when the flight files at or above that top, because the SOP interim table applies only where no top altitude is published

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 4 (b); ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: CLIMB VIA SID EXCEPT MAINTAIN (altitude) — the SID has published crossing restrictions and the altitude to maintain is not its published top: either no top altitude is published and an SOP interim altitude applies, or the flight files below the published top

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 5; ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: MAINTAIN (altitude) — the SID has no published crossing restrictions, or is a radar-vector SID or has a radar-vector segment

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 3 / SFO ATCT SOP 2-2 c iv; ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: EXPECT (filed altitude) (minutes) MINUTES AFTER DEPARTURE — spoken when the filed altitude is above the altitude cleared to and the SID chart does not itself publish the expect note; three minutes when a non-standard interim altitude is issued (SFO ATCT SOP 2-2 c iv)

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference; FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 3
phraseologyRules.text: EXPECT AMENDED (altitude) (minutes) MINUTES AFTER DEPARTURE — spoken when the controller amended the final altitude from what was filed; the SID chart's own expect note covers only the filed altitude, so this clause is spoken even where the chart publishes one

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA senior staff via the user, 2026-09-16; FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 c 3
phraseologyRules.text: EXPECT (filed altitude) (minutes) MINUTES AFTER DEPARTURE spoken where the SID chart already publishes that note is not wrong, only longer than it needs to be: it repeats what the chart tells the pilot. Graded acceptable when the delay spoken is the chart's, and a miss otherwise

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA practice via the user, 2026-09-16 (SKW2345 amendment plan)
phraseologyRules.text: (altitude) WILL BE YOUR FINAL — spoken in place of the expect clause when the controller amended the final altitude and the clearance climbs the flight straight to it, speaking that altitude (CLIMB VIA SID EXCEPT MAINTAIN or MAINTAIN at the amended altitude): there is nothing further to expect, so the pilot is told the altitude just assigned is the final one. A plain CLIMB VIA SID speaks no altitude of its own, so the amended expect clause is spoken there instead, even where the published top altitude is the amended one. EXPECT AMENDED (altitude) (minutes) MINUTES AFTER DEPARTURE spoken there instead is acceptable, only longer than it needs to be, at the delay the amended clause would carry

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-3-2 a; ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference
phraseologyRules.text: CLEARED TO (destination) AIRPORT — the clearance limit is the destination airport

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-5-2 Flight Direction (TBL 4-5-1); 14 CFR 91.179
phraseologyRules.text: Below FL290 a magnetic course of 0 through 179 degrees takes the odd thousands and 180 through 359 the even thousands, FL290 through FL410 the same rule by flight level (FL310, FL330 against FL320, FL340), and above FL410 the 4,000-ft series: FL450 and FL490 for 0 through 179, FL430 and FL470 for 180 through 359

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-5-2 Flight Direction (TBL 4-5-1, one way routes); user ruling 2026-09-16 (FDX3875 amendment plan)
phraseologyRules.text: A one-way route carries no opposing traffic, so the direction-of-flight rule has nothing to separate on it: any cardinal altitude or flight level at or below FL410 is assigned on any course, and above FL410 any odd cardinal flight level (FL430, FL450). The Pacific oceanic routes the Bay departs on are one-way, so a westbound flight to Hawaii keeps the odd level it filed

phraseologyRules.source: 14 CFR 91.180 and part 91 appendix G; AIM 4-6-1 (RVSM mandate, FL290-FL410 inclusive); FAA JO 7110.65 4-5-1 b
phraseologyRules.text: FL290 through FL410 inclusive is RVSM airspace, so an aircraft whose equipment suffix does not carry RVSM approval is not assigned an altitude in that band

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference; user ruling 2026-09-17 (free-text entry)
phraseologyRules.text: THEN AS FILED spoken where the route is read to its end — nothing is filed after the last fix read, so the reading closes on DIRECT — is acceptable, not wrong: the pilot flies the same route either way, but R-THEN-AS-FILED reads such a route in full

phraseologyRules.source: ZOA CRAFT Phraseology reference; user ruling 2026-09-17 (free-text entry)
phraseologyRules.text: Reading the whole of an amended or built route, where the clearance hands it over as filed from the fix the two routes run together from (R-THEN-AS-FILED), is acceptable, not wrong: the pilot is cleared along the same route, only at greater length than the clearance needs

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 2-5-2; user ruling 2026-09-17 (free-text entry)
phraseologyRules.text: The facility word spoken after a fix the clearance reads bare (R-AS-FILED) is as right as the bare name: CONCORD VOR, THEN AS FILED names the same navaid as CONCORD, THEN AS FILED

phraseologyRules.source: user ruling 2026-09-17 (free-text entry)
phraseologyRules.text: Words the phraseology does not have (climb via THE SID, cleared to THE Seattle airport, YOUR departure frequency WILL BE) make an element acceptable rather than right: every value and every required word is there, but the transmission is longer than it needs to be. A required word left out is a miss

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 4-2-1; user ruling 2026-09-17 (free-text entry)
phraseologyRules.text: Clearance items are issued in the order 7110.65 4-2-1 lists them: clearance limit, departure procedure or vectors, route, altitude, then frequency and beacon code. An element read out of that order is a miss, and the elements marked are the fewest whose removal leaves the rest in order

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 2-4-16 (TBL 2-4-1); user ruling 2026-09-17 (free-text entry)
phraseologyRules.text: Digits are spoken in the ICAO pronunciation, the digit 9 as NINER: TREE, FIFE, FOWER and the other ICAO forms are as right as the plain words, but NINE said for the digit is a miss. A procedure's name is exempt, because it is spoken as its chart name (Coast Nine)

phraseologyRules.source: FAA JO 7110.65 2-4-17 b 2 (a) and its note; user ruling 2026-09-17 (free-text entry)
phraseologyRules.text: A number the clearance speaks digit by digit (an altitude, a frequency, the beacon code, a heading, the runway, the expect minutes) is right only in digit form: ONE ZERO THOUSAND. The group form may follow the digits as a restatement for clarity (ONE ZERO THOUSAND, TEN THOUSAND, or ONE ZERO TEN THOUSAND), which is acceptable but longer than it needs to be; the group form alone (TEN THOUSAND) is a miss. A number typed in figures is right

phraseologyRules.source: SFO ATCT SOP 1-7; user review 2026-09-15 (N483KA)
phraseologyRules.text: The configuration departs this aircraft class from this runway by default, before the direction-of-turn split: in 28/01, props and turboprops depart 28R at intersection Echo, a short taxi from the north ramp

phraseologyRules.source: SFO ATCT SOP 2-1 e; user review 2026-09-15 (FDX1563, UPS2896)
phraseologyRules.text: Oceanic, Far East and cargo flights usually need 28L/R for performance; when 01 is the advertised departure runway they may be issued 28L/R and the matching SID. A strip remark requesting the 28s, or a cargo or heavy flight filing a 28-only SID, is honoured

phraseologyRules.source: S1-SFO-0 CBT, Runway Assignment: 28/01 1L or 1R?
phraseologyRules.text: The departure runway follows the first turn: right turn (northbound SIDs) 1R, left turn (southbound SIDs) 1L, which allows simultaneous parallel departures; the same table splits the 28s and the SFOE families

phraseologyRules.source: SFO ATCT SOP 1-7
phraseologyRules.text: The configuration departs a single runway of this family for this aircraft class, so that runway is issued

Landing and departing runways 28, straight out (TRUKN DP not in use)

sids.note: Chart publishes no named transitions; CIFP codes vector transitions ALCOA BEBOP ENI OAK OSI SAU SGD. Expect vector to assigned route/fix after NORMM (28) / OSI (10, 19) / on SFO R-350 (01).
CBT: BAART leads to BEBOP; pilots sometimes file GNNRR BEBOP. Top altitude 3000 published -> climb via SID.
Conventional pilot-nav SID with crossing restrictions; DME and RADAR required. CBT: climb via SID except maintain (28: 3000; 10: J 15000, P/T 5000).

Radar-vector SID; the FAA does not code it in CIFP. Runway 28: SFO R-281 to NORMM then vectors (no restriction -> maintain 3,000). Runway 01: heading 033 or assigned, cross SFO 6 DME at or above 3000 for vectors (a crossing restriction -> climb via SID except maintain; S1-SFO-0 CBT agrees). The chart reads 'expect further clearance to filed altitude 10 minutes after departure' (user 2026-09-16: the chart covers the clause).
Successor to the OFFSH# departure described in the 2023 CBT (MCKEY -> YYUNG). Left turn off the 01s, so 1L.
CBT: RWY 1L only, so it can depart in parallel with TRUKN# on 1R.
CBT: RWY 28R/L and RWY 1R (right turn); 1R allows simultaneous parallel departures with 1L SSTIK#/SEGUL#.
